name: A hybrid model's KV cost depends entirely on how many layers are full attention, and when config gives a GROUP SIZE rather than an index list, reading the group size as the layer count inflates the KV figure several-fold
symptom: ling-3-0-flash recorded kv_cache_bytes_per_token 23040, overstating the real figure 8064 by 2.86x (20 attention layers used where 7 are real). The record had attention_layer_indices and layer_types left null, which is the visible symptom: an author could not find the layer list in config and substituted a number that looked plausible. The consequence was not cosmetic. Ling-3.0-Flash advertises max_position_embeddings 262144; at 23040 B/token one 256k sequence needs 5.60 GiB of KV, at 8064 it needs 2.00 GiB. The old figure is the difference between a 256k request fitting alongside the weights on a single 80GB-class card and not fitting at all, so the error inverted the answer to the only question this field exists to answer.
root_cause: config.json for this family does not enumerate the attention layers. It publishes num_hidden_layers 42 and layer_group_size 6, and the split is implied by a rule implemented in modeling_bailing_moe_v3.py at the layer-construction site: attention_layer_type = 'attention' if (layer_idx + 1) % layer_group_size == 0 or layer_idx >= num_hidden_layers // layer_group_size * layer_group_size else 'linear_attention'. Over 42 layers at group size 6 that yields attention at 0-based indices 5, 11, 17, 23, 29, 35, 41 - seven layers. The recorded 20 is a different config field entirely: max_window_layers is 20, which is a WINDOW cap on the attention layers, not a count of them. So the failure is a field-semantics mix-up between two integers in the same file, both small and both plausible as a layer count. The same trap is waiting in every hybrid in this repo: config publishes at least three integers that look like layer counts (num_hidden_layers, max_window_layers, and a group size or interval), and only one of them is the answer.
workaround: When config gives a group size, interval or pattern instead of an index list, derive the index list from the rule in the modeling code and RECORD it in attention_layer_indices and layer_types rather than leaving them null. A null split on a hybrid record is the tell that the KV figure was not derived. Cross-check against a sibling: kimi-linear-48b-a3b is the same KDA+MLA design and its config DOES enumerate linear_attn_config.full_attn_layers [4,8,12,16,20,24,27] = 7 of 27 layers, giving 7 x 576 x 2 = 8,064 B/token - identical to the corrected Ling figure, which is the consistency check that identified 23,040 as underivable. For weight-level confirmation without modeling code, count layers carrying q_proj in model.safetensors.index.json.
notes:
CORRECTED ARITHMETIC for ling-3-0-flash: 7 attention layers x (kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope_head_dim 64) x 2 bytes (bf16) = 7 x 576 x 2 = 8,064 B/token (7.9 KiB/token). attention_layer_indices [5,11,17,23,29,35,41] and a 42-entry layer_types are now recorded, where both were previously null. FAMILY-WIDE CHECK, every hybrid in this repo re-derived from its own config: kimi-k3 (linear_attn_config.full_attn_layers = 24 of 93) 24 x 576 x 2 = 27,648 CORRECT as recorded; kimi-linear-48b-a3b 7 of 27 = 8,064 CORRECT; granite-4-0-h-tiny (layer_types, attention at 5,15,25,35 = 4 of 40) 4 x 4 x 128 x 2 x 2 = 8,192 CORRECT as recorded, and this record is the counter-example that proves the head-dim lesson was already learned once: its head_dim 128 comes from hidden_size 1536 / num_attention_heads 12 = 128, not from the string 'h-tiny' in the name; nemotron-h-8b-base-8k 4 of 52 = 16,384 CORRECT, with the split confirmed against the safetensors index (backbone.layers.7/18/29/40 carry mixer.q_proj, all 52 carry mixer.*) because that config's hybrid_override_pattern string is TRUNCATED at 25 characters and does not itself cover 52 layers; lfm2-1-2b and lfm2-5-1-2b-instruct (full_attn_idxs [2,5,8,10,12,14] = 6 of 16) correctly record 0 for a bounded-not-growing cache with the 12,288 B/token attention slice spelled out in notes; zamba-7b (layers_block_type 'hybrid' at 2,7,13,19,25,31,37,43,49,55,61,67,73 = 13 of 76) 2 x 13 x 16 x 232 x 2 = 193,024 CORRECT as recorded; falcon-h1-7b-base is the deliberate exception - config sets attn_layer_indices null and the safetensors index shows every one of 44 layers carrying BOTH self_attn and mamba tensors, so attention runs in PARALLEL with the SSM on every layer, attention_layer_indices [0..43] is correct, and 2 x 44 x 2 x 128 x 2 = 45,056 stands. That last one is the mirror image of this bug: for a parallel hybrid the KV cache does NOT shrink, and a reader who assumed 'hybrid implies few attention layers' would under-budget it by the full 44/4 factor.

THE TWO CONVENTIONS IN THIS REPO, WHICH LOOK LIKE AN INCONSISTENCY BUT ARE NOT, AND WHICH AN AUDITOR MUST KNOW BEFORE RECOMPUTING ANY OF THESE FIGURES. Class 1 - linear/SSM hybrids (Gated DeltaNet, KDA, Mamba): the non-attention layers hold a FIXED-SIZE recurrent state and no growing KV cache at all, so the per-token figure counts ONLY the attention layers. Every record in this class does this: kimi-k3 24 of 93 = 27,648; kimi-linear 7 of 27 = 8,064; qwen3-5-35b-a3b 10 of 40 = 20,480; qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct 12 of 48 = 24,576; granite-4-0-h-tiny 4 of 40 = 8,192; nemotron-h 4 of 52 = 16,384; and the corrected ling-3-0-flash 7 of 42 = 8,064. Class 2 - sliding-window hybrids where EVERY layer still carries a KV cache (Gemma 2, Gemma 3n, GPT-OSS, OLMo 3, Ministral): the per-token figure counts ALL layers, i.e. the unbounded worst case, and each of those records states the sliding-window caveat in its notes so a reader can discount it. gemma-2-9b 42 x 8 x 256 x 2 x 2 = 344,064 rather than 172,032; gpt-oss-20b 24 rather than 12 layers; olmo-3-7b 32 rather than 8; ministral-8b 36 rather than 9; gemma-3n-e2b 30 rather than 6. A recomputation that silently applies Class 1 logic to a Class 2 model will report a 2x-5x 'mismatch' that is really just the two conventions meeting, and the correct response is to check the notes rather than to change the number. Class 2 is the right choice there because the window is a runtime setting an operator may widen or disable, so the per-token figure should describe the ceiling. The genuinely wrong records are the ones where the count is not derivable from config under EITHER convention - ling-3-0-flash's 20 came from max_window_layers, a third field entirely, and matched neither.
